One Counter, Four Tablets: How to Organize a Delivery App Station

Picture the Friday dinner rush at a ghost kitchen. One tablet is propped against the receipt printer. Another is balanced on top of a stack of to-go bags. A third is flat on the counter, screen-down, because someone needed the space. The fourth is plugged in near the fryer because that was the only outlet. An order comes in on the one that is face-down. Nobody sees it for four minutes. The customer cancels.

That scenario plays out in quick-service restaurants, food halls, and pickup counters every weekend. The fix is not a new workflow or a new hire. It is a dedicated multi-tablet stand for restaurant delivery operations that puts every screen in one place, at eye level, with cables managed and roles assigned before the rush starts.

Quick Answer

A four-tablet tower stand consolidates your delivery app tablets and POS into a single vertical footprint, keeps every screen visible to staff, and eliminates the counter clutter that causes missed orders. iBOLT makes three configurations: a freestanding tower, a counter-clamp version, and a wall-mount version, all holding up to four tablets from 7 to 11 inches.

Why Scattered Tablets Cost You Orders

Each major delivery platform expects its tablet to stay active and visible. DoorDash notes that the merchant tablet is used for order and store management tasks in real time, meaning a tablet that is buried or asleep is a tablet that is not working. Uber Eats states that its Orders app needs to stay visible in the foreground and can pause after missed orders or offline time. Grubhub's tablet setup guidance reinforces that a properly installed tablet is the foundation of reliable order flow.

When tablets are scattered, staff have to physically scan the counter to check for new orders. During a rush, that scan does not always happen. A mounted station removes the scan entirely because every screen is in the same sightline.

Before you buy a stand, answer three questions: How much counter space can you dedicate? Is a permanent installation acceptable? And where does your staff naturally look during service? The table below maps those answers to the right iBOLT setup.

Adding a Cashier-Facing POS Phone Station

Not every station is tablet-only. Many QSR and food hall setups run a phone-based POS or a loyalty app on a separate device at the register. The iBOLT Phone Dock'n Lock Dual POS Stand handles that scenario. It is a drill-base mount with a 9-inch pole and two locking phone holders, one facing the cashier and one facing the customer. The holders fit phones and cases between 4.8 and 7.25 inches tall and 2.25 and 3.75 inches wide. The locking design prevents unauthorized removal, which matters in a high-traffic pickup environment.

iBOLT Phone Dock'n Lock Dual POS Stand - Secure Dual-Device Mount for Point of Sale Systems - $115.00

Cable and Charging Discipline

A mounted tablet that runs out of battery is no better than a tablet on the floor. When you install any of the TabDock towers, run charging cables along the pole before you seat the tablets. Use cable ties or adhesive clips to keep cords from draping across the counter. Assign one power strip or USB charging hub directly below or behind the tower so every cable has a short, clean path. Label each cable at the plug end with the platform name so staff can reconnect quickly after cleaning.

Role Assignment: Which Screen Goes Where

Once the hardware is in place, assign a fixed position to each platform and post a small label on the holder. Staff should never have to read the screen to know which app they are looking at. A common arrangement for a four-tablet station: position one at top-left for your highest-volume delivery platform, position two at top-right for the second platform, position three at bottom-left for the third platform or a kitchen display, and position four at bottom-right for your POS or order management system. Consistency across shifts reduces the chance that an order sits unacknowledged because a new team member was looking at the wrong screen.

Frequently Asked Questions

What tablet sizes fit the iBOLT TabDock towers?

All three TabDock four-tablet configurations hold tablets from 7 to 11 inches. Each holder has four points of contact and rotates 360 degrees for portrait or landscape orientation.

Can I install the clamp mount without drilling?

Yes. The TabDock POS Clamp Mount attaches to counter edges up to 2.5 inches wide without any drilling. A drill base is included if you want a permanent installation later.

Is the wall mount difficult to install?

The TabDock POS Wall Mount kit includes all hardware, adapters, and an extension pole. The pole adjusts from 17.5 to 28.5 inches, so you can set the screen height before committing to final screw placement.

Does the Dual POS Stand work with phone cases on?

Yes. The Phone Dock'n Lock Dual POS Stand holders accommodate phones and cases between 4.8 and 7.25 inches tall and 2.25 and 3.75 inches wide, covering most standard phone and case combinations.

Will a mounted tablet actually reduce missed orders?

A mount improves screen visibility, keeps devices in a consistent location, and supports charging discipline. Those factors reduce the conditions that lead to missed orders, but operational results depend on staffing, app settings, and kitchen workflow as well.
